verdict.summary: The exact v3 successor closes the v2 self-authenticating-gate rejection within its stated trusted-host Python-model boundary. A fieldless context supplies no authority; one selected out-of-band host authority binds a canonical exactly-once reservation to the exact newly allocated object and projects only by its own root-local identity binding. Independent probes rejected fresh and same-key second-authority contexts, a genuinely populated caller registry, every direct/duplicate/unreserved exact-type object, copy and serialization, and all six declared construction routes without selected-authority state change. The exact OP2 projection, authenticated source-buffer execution, closed v3-to-v2 delta, dependency closure, malformed/duplicate totality, and all v1/v2 dispositions also reconstruct. Production Rust ownership and durable atomicity remain unexecuted and this PASS does not apply, bind, or seal the candidate.

findingDispositionAssessment.basis: The normal dependency path hashes one exact source buffer and compiles/executes that buffer. Reviewer-authored actual-helper probes independently proved that an authentic source plus timestamp-valid malicious pyc executes only authentic source, and that wrong-hash source is rejected before its side effect.

The context is fieldless and supplies no projection fact. Direct object.__new__, duplicate, unreserved, leak, slot, copy, serialization, second-root, and caller-registry probes all reject at the selected authority without state change.

No v2 gate, context accessor, or module mint helper remains. The selected authority's out-of-band exact-object registry is the provenance root, and contexts from a separately populated authority reject even when both roots reserve the same canonical key.

The substitute registry was independently confirmed nonempty and mapped a canonical key to the exact forged object. Supplying it was rejected as TRUSTED_AUTHORITY_PARAMETER_FORBIDDEN; a separate populated authority was also exercised.

Independent AST and behavior review found no module-global selected authority, context, token, gate, mint registry, v2 mint helper, or state writer outside authority initialization/begin. More importantly, independently constructed equivalent authorities cannot project under the selected root. Direct allocation sites used by negative fixtures do exist intentionally but cannot enter selected state; the operative exclusivity claim is authority-state binding, not allocation impossibility.

Caller, sink, provider, stage, profile, and projection adapter are six distinct retained functions with six distinct code objects; each directly allocates an exact-type lookalike and independently rejects without selected-state change.

Both the candidate's advanced tests and this review's malicious-pyc/wrong-hash probes call the actual _exec_pinned_source helper used by normal loading; no duplicate source-execution implementation is the evidence path.
